claims.text: THE PUBLIC TAXONOMY HAS BEEN NARROWING. DoD Directive 5205.07, 'Special Access Program Policy', was reissued effective 12 September 2024 and cancels the 1 July 2010 version. The full public text of the 2024 directive - purpose, applicability, policy, all thirteen responsibility assignments, the governance section, the complete glossary and the reference list - contains no occurrence of the words 'waived' or 'unacknowledged' at all. The directive that used to define the waived category no longer mentions it; the taxonomy now survives publicly only in the subordinate instruction, DoDI 5205.11. Anyone checking only the directive would conclude the category no longer exists.

claims.sourceText: Inference from the structure of 10 U.S.C. 119 and DoDD 5205.07
claims.text: The allegation of a concealed legacy recovery program is, in legal terms, an allegation about a single line of the United States Code: that 10 U.S.C. 119(e) has been used to reduce congressional knowledge of a materials exploitation activity to eight members, or that the activity was never entered into the SAP system at all. Reasoning: those are the only two possibilities the statutory scheme allows.

edges.note: Defined in DoD Directive 5205.07 and DoD Manual 5205.07 Volume 1 as a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense relieving the defence security agency of its National Industrial Security Program oversight responsibilities at a contractor facility. It is the structural seam at which a programme held at a company stops being visible to any government security official outside the programme.

edges.label: the statutory oversight scheme, and the exception written into it
edges.note: Under 10 U.S.C. 119 the Secretary must report annually by 1 March to the four defense committees on every special access program, with a brief description, major milestones and costs - and under 119(e) may waive any of that on a case-by-case basis. The scheme and its exception are the same statute, which is why oversight belongs on the structural map rather than outside it.

edges.label: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.a(3) - waived-SAP access limited to chair, ranking member, staff directors and one security manager
edges.note: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs,' effective 12 September 2024, para. 7.2.a(3): 'Only the chair, the ranking member, the staff directors, and one designated security manager of the defense and intelligence committees will be authorized access to waived DoD SAPs within their committee's respective oversight jurisdiction. Requests to access additional members of Congress or professional staff must be approved by the Secretary of Defense or Deputy Secretary of Defense.' This is materially wider than 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) on two axes: it admits committee staff directors and a security manager, and it extends to the intelligence committees, which have no entitlement under section 119. Any board text asserting that the twelve have no staff who can read the material should be corrected against this paragraph. Para. 7.2.b confirms that ordinary members of the defense and intelligence committees are authorised access to all DoD SAPs in their jurisdiction 'except for waived programs.'

edges.label: DoDI 5205.11 retains the acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived taxonomy the 2024 directive omitted
edges.note: DoDI 5205.11 para. 1.2.f, effective the same day as the reissued DoDD 5205.07: 'The Secretary of Defense may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived" when it is determined that using standard procedures for reporting to Congress would adversely affect national security, pursuant to Section 119 of Title 10, United States Code. Waived SAPs remain subject to congressional oversight.' The glossary retains definitions of acknowledged SAP, unacknowledged SAP, SAP type and waived SAP, the last defined as 'A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable ... An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.' The taxonomy was therefore not retired in September 2024; it was moved down one level from the directive into the instruction. Para. 3 further requires the SAP Oversight Committee's annual review to assess 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status' - an internal executive-branch review with no congressional trigger and no analogue in section 119.

edges.note: Same policy instrument, two issuances, and the programmatic relation is what CHANGED between them - which is not the same fact as the supersession recorded on the temporal edge. The 2010 directive's glossary defines 'carve-out' as 'a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its National Industrial Security Program oversight', and its Enclosure 2 para 5 restates the statutory waiver in policy. A full-text pass of the 12 September 2024 reissue finds no occurrence of 'carve-out', 'waived' or 'unacknowledged' at all. The vocabulary the earlier directive defined is simply absent from the later one. Note what that does and does not establish: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) still carries the carve-out in codified regulation, and still points at DoDD 5205.07 by name, so the mechanism did not end when the words left the directive.
